question: In which year did Jyotiba Phule open a school for girls which was the first girls school ever in the country? (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: 1858
1838
1868
1848
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1848

Explanation:
Jyotiba Phule opened the country's first girls' school in Pune in 1848. He was a prominent Indian social reformer, educationist, and writer who worked for the upliftment of women and Dalits. His wife, Savitribai Phule, served as the first female teacher at this school. The school was established during British rule and faced severe opposition from orthodox sections of society. Phule also founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873, an organization promoting social equality. His efforts laid the foundation for women's education in India.

☛ Famous book by Jyotiba Phule → Gulamgiri
question_hi: ज्योतिबा फुले ने किस वर्ष लड़कियों के लिए एक स्कूल खोला था जो देश का पहला बालिका स्कूल था? (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 2)

1838

1848

Explanation:

question: When did Swami Vivekananda propagate the real philosophy and culture of India to the world at the Parliament of the World’s Religions in Chicago? (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: 1893
1853
1873
1883

Explanation:
Swami Vivekananda participated in the World's Parliament of Religions held in Chicago, USA in September 1893. He later founded the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897. His speech emphasized universal brotherhood and the essence of Hinduism.

Explanation:

question: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan, who founded the organisation of non-violent revolutionaries known as 'Red Shirts', was known by the name of ____ (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Political Guru of Gandhi
Frontier Gandhi
Shaheed-e-Azam
Bismarck of India
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Frontier Gandhi

Explanation:
Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan was known as Frontier Gandhi. He was a non-violent freedom fighter who founded the Khudai Khidmatgar (Red Shirts) movement in the North-West Frontier Province (now Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa). The movement was based on non-violence and satyagraha, inspired by Mahatma Gandhi's ideals. He united the Pashtuns against British rule and played a key role in the Quit India Movement. Due to his commitment to non-violence, he was respectfully called Frontier Gandhi. He opposed the partition of India and later worked for human rights in Pakistan.

☛ Province associated with Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan → North-West Frontier Province
question_hi: खान अब्दुल गफ्फार खान, जिन्होंने 'रेड शर्ट्स' के नाम से जाने जाने वाले अहिंसक क्रांतिकारियों के संगठन की स्थापना की थी, उन्हें ____ के नाम से जाना जाता था। (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 2)

सीमांत गांधी
शहीद-ए-आजम
भारत के बिस्मार्क
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है सीमांत गांधी

Explanation:
खान अब्दुल गफ्फार खान को सीमांत गांधी के नाम से जाना जाता था। वे एक अहिंसक स्वतंत्रता सेनानी थे जिन्होंने उत्तर-पश्चिम सीमांत प्रांत (वर्तमान खैबर-पख्तूनख्वा) में खुदाई खिदमतगार (रेड शर्ट्स) आंदोलन की स्थापना की। यह आंदोलन अहिंसा और सत्याग्रह पर आधारित था, जो महात्मा गांधी के विचारों से प्रेरित था। उन्होंने ब्रिटिश शासन के खिलाफ पश्तूनों को एकजुट किया और भारत छोड़ो आंदोलन में महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाई। उनके अहिंसक संघर्ष के कारण उन्हें गांधी जी के सम्मान में सीमांत गांधी कहा जाता है। वे पाकिस्तान के निर्माण के विरोधी थे और बाद में पाकिस्तान में मानवाधिकारों के लिए काम किया।

question: What was the name of the Captain of the Awadh Military Police who had been given protection by his Indian subordinates during the mutiny of 1857?  (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Captain Auckland
Captain Savarkar
Captain Hearsey

solution:

Explanation:
During the mutiny of 1857, Captain Hearsey was the Captain of the Awadh Military Police. He was given protection by his Indian subordinates because he was kind and fair to his soldiers. question: In 1930, who in his most famous speech stressed the creation of a Muslim state in North West India? (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Khuzaima Qutbuddin
Ali Kutty Musliyar
Sir Muhammad Iqbal
Syed Ali Akhtar Rizvi
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Sir Muhammad Iqbal

Explanation:
In 1930, Allama Iqbal in his famous Allahabad address stressed the creation of a Muslim state in North West India. This speech was delivered at the annual session of the Muslim League. Iqbal proposed merging Punjab, NWFP, Sindh, and Balochistan into a separate Muslim state. He believed Muslims in India were a distinct nation and needed autonomy. Although he did not use the word 'Pakistan', his ideas laid the foundation for the Two-Nation Theory and the Pakistan movement.

Explanation:
1930 में अल्लामा इक़बाल ने अपने इलाहाबाद भाषण में उत्तर-पश्चिम भारत में एक मुस्लिम राज्य के निर्माण पर बल दिया था। यह भाषण मुस्लिम लीग के वार्षिक अधिवेशन में दिया गया था। इक़बाल ने पंजाब, NWFP, सिंध और बलूचिस्तान को मिलाकर एक अलग मुस्लिम राज्य का सुझाव दिया। उनका मानना था कि भारत में मुसलमान एक अलग राष्ट्र हैं और उन्हें स्वायत्तता की आवश्यकता है। हालांकि उन्होंने 'पाकिस्तान' शब्द का प्रयोग नहीं किया, लेकिन उनके विचारों ने द्विराष्ट्र सिद्धांत और पाकिस्तान आंदोलन की नींव रखी।

question: Which of the following was NOT a demand of the extremists? (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Complete Swaraj
Promotion of Swadeshi industries
Complete independence
Constitutional reforms
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Constitutional reforms

Explanation:
The Extremists (1905-1918) were the militant faction of the Indian National Movement, led by Bal Gangadhar Tilak, Lala Lajpat Rai, and Bipin Chandra Pal. Their key demands included Complete Swaraj (self-rule), Promotion of Swadeshi industries, and Complete independence. They advocated direct action and boycott against British rule. In contrast, Constitutional reforms was a demand of the Moderates, who sought gradual reforms from the British government. The Extremists believed constitutional reforms were inadequate and emphasized Swaraj and independence. Therefore, constitutional reforms was not a demand of the Extremists.

☛ What was the main goal of the Extremists? → Complete Swaraj
☛ What was the main difference between Moderates and Extremists? → Moderates wanted constitutional reforms; Extremists wanted complete independence
☛ What does Swadeshi mean? → Use of domestically made products and boycott of foreign goods
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सी गरमपंथियों की मांग नहीं थी? (RPF Constable 2024 (02/03/2025) Shift 3)
options_hi: पूर्ण स्वराज
स्वदेशी उद्योगों का प्रचार
पूर्ण स्वतंत्रता
संवैधानिक सुधार
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है संवैधानिक सुधार

Explanation:
गरमपंथी (1905-1918) भारतीय राष्ट्रीय आंदोलन के उग्रवादी धड़े थे, जिनका नेतृत्व बाल गंगाधर तिलक, लाला लाजपत राय और बिपिन चंद्र पाल ने किया। उनकी प्रमुख मांगें थीं: पूर्ण स्वराज (स्वशासन), स्वदेशी उद्योगों का प्रचार, और पूर्ण स्वतंत्रता। वे ब्रिटिश शासन के खिलाफ सीधे कार्रवाई और बहिष्कार के पक्षधर थे। दूसरी ओर, संवैधानिक सुधार नरमपंथियों (मॉडरेट्स) की मांग थी, जो ब्रिटिश सरकार से चरणबद्ध सुधार चाहते थे। गरमपंथियों का मानना था कि संवैधानिक सुधार पर्याप्त नहीं हैं और उन्होंने स्वराज और स्वतंत्रता पर जोर दिया। इस प्रकार, संवैधानिक सुधार गरमपंथियों की मांग नहीं थी।

question: During which movement in 1920 did Mahatma Gandhi call for the boycott of foreign clothes in West Godavari? (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 1)
options: Quit India Movement
Ghadar Movement
Non-cooperation Movement
Civil Disobedience Movement
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Non-cooperation Movement

Explanation:
In 1920, Mahatma Gandhi called for the boycott of foreign clothes in West Godavari during the Non-cooperation Movement. This movement, launched in August 1920, aimed at non-violent resistance against British rule. Gandhi made the boycott of foreign cloth a part of the Swadeshi movement, which aimed to strengthen the Indian economy and cripple the British textile industry. During the movement, people surrendered government titles and boycotted government institutions. In West Godavari, Gandhi addressed public meetings and urged people to burn foreign clothes in bonfires. The Non-cooperation Movement was suspended in 1922 after the Chauri Chaura incident, which turned violent. This movement marked a significant phase in India's freedom struggle by mobilizing mass participation.

question:

question: After the revolt of 1857, the title of 'Empress of India' was given to the Queen of England in: (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: 1887
1857
1877
1861
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1877

Explanation:
After the Revolt of 1857, the British government transferred the administration of India from the East India Company to the British Crown through the Government of India Act 1858. Queen Victoria assumed direct rule over India. On 1 May 1876, she decided to adopt the title of 'Empress of India', and it was formally proclaimed at the Delhi Durbar on 1 January 1877. The title was conferred by the Royal Titles Act 1876. The proclamation was made by the then Viceroy of India, Lord Lytton. The title aimed to strengthen British sovereignty over Indian princely states and subjects, and to symbolically unite India under the British Empire.

question: Who wrote the book 'The Indian War of Independence' related to Indian nationalist history of the 1857 revolt? (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 2)

Sardar Patel
Subhash Chandra Bose
V D Savarkar
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is V D Savarkar

Explanation:
V D Savarkar wrote 'The Indian War of Independence 1857' in 1909. The book described the 1857 revolt as India's first war of independence. It was critical of British rule and was banned in India. Savarkar argued that the revolt was not just a sepoy mutiny but a result of national consciousness. The book played a key role in inspiring Indian nationalists.

question: When did Sir Syed Ahmed Khan find the Scientific Society to translate English books on science and other subjects into Urdu? (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: 1852
1872
1882
1864
solution:

Explanation:
Sir Syed Ahmed Khan established the Scientific Society in 1864 with the aim of translating English books, especially on science and other subjects, into Urdu. The society was first set up in Ghazipur and later shifted to Aligarh. Its primary objective was to introduce modern science and Western knowledge to Indian Muslims. Through this initiative, Sir Syed sought to bring educational reforms. The Scientific Society published translations of important works, which helped disseminate scientific knowledge in the Urdu language. This was a crucial part of Sir Syed's educational movement, which eventually led to the establishment of the Aligarh Muslim University.

question: Who among the following started the Bhoodan Movement in  April 1951 with the aim of bringing about fundamental social and economic changes in the society through peaceful means? (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Vallabhbhai Patel
Vinayak Damodar Savarkar
Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan
Acharya Vinoba Bhave
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Acharya Vinoba Bhave

Explanation:
The Bhoodan Movement was started in April 1951 by Acharya Vinoba Bhave. It was a Gandhian movement aimed at bringing about fundamental social and economic changes through peaceful means. Vinoba Bhave was considered the spiritual successor of Mahatma Gandhi. The movement involved voluntary donation of land by wealthy landowners to the landless poor. It sought to address the problem of land inequality and promote social justice without conflict. The movement was based on the principles of non-violence and voluntary action. Vinoba Bhave also promoted the concept of Gram Swaraj through this movement. The Bhoodan Movement is a landmark in India's post-independence land reform efforts.

☛ Year of initiation → 1951
☛ Basis of the movement → Non-violence and voluntary donation
☛ Vinoba Bhave was the successor of → Mahatma Gandhi
☛ Objective of the movement → Land reform and social change
question_hi: अप्रैल 1951 में निम्नलिखित में से किसने शांतिपूर्ण तरीकों से समाज में मूलभूत सामाजिक और आर्थिक परिवर्तन लाने के उद्देश्य से भूदान आंदोलन शुरू किया था? (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 2)

question: Which of the following is NOT the provision of the Government of India Act, 1858? (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 2)
options: Board of Control and Court of Directors were abolished.
Armed forces of the company were transferred to the Crown.
The 'Governor General of India' designation was changed to the 'Viceroy of India'.
Law Member was made a full member of the Executive Council of the Governor General.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Law Member was made a full member of the Executive Council of the Governor General.

Explanation:
The Government of India Act, 1858 ended the rule of the East India Company and brought India directly under the British Crown. Its key provisions included abolishing the Board of Control and Court of Directors, transferring the company's armed forces to the Crown, and changing the title of Governor General of India to Viceroy of India. However, making the Law Member a full member of the Executive Council was a provision of the Charter Act of 1853, not the 1858 Act. The 1853 Act had added a Law Member to the Governor General's council. Therefore, Option 4 is not a provision of the 1858 Act.

☛ Which bodies were abolished by the 1858 Act? → Board of Control and Court of Directors
☛ What was the new title of the Governor General after 1858? → Viceroy
☛ To whom were the company's armed forces transferred by the 1858 Act? → The Crown
☛ Which rule began in India with the 1858 Act? → Direct rule of the Crown
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन-सा 1858 के भारत सरकार अधिनियम का प्रावधान नहीं है? (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 2)
options_hi: नियंत्रण बोर्ड और निदेशक न्यायालय को समाप्त कर दिया गया था।
कंपनी के सशस्त्र बल क्राउन को हस्तांतरित कर दिए गए थे।
भारत के 'गवर्नर जनरल' पदनाम को बदलकर 'भारत का वायसराय' कर दिया गया था।
विधि सदस्य को गवर्नर जनरल की कार्यकारी परिषद का पूर्ण सदस्य बनाया गया था।
solution_hi:
Solution: सही उत्तर है विधि सदस्य को गवर्नर जनरल की कार्यकारी परिषद का पूर्ण सदस्य बनाया गया था।

Explanation:
1858 का भारत सरकार अधिनियम भारत में ईस्ट इंडिया कंपनी के शासन को समाप्त करके इसे सीधे ब्रिटिश क्राउन के अधीन लाया। इस अधिनियम के प्रमुख प्रावधान थे: नियंत्रण बोर्ड और निदेशक न्यायालय को समाप्त करना, कंपनी की सशस्त्र सेनाओं को क्राउन को हस्तांतरित करना, और भारत के गवर्नर जनरल के पदनाम को भारत के वायसराय में बदलना। हालांकि, विधि सदस्य को कार्यकारी परिषद का पूर्ण सदस्य बनाने का प्रावधान 1853 का चार्टर अधिनियम था, न कि 1858 का अधिनियम। 1853 के चार्टर अधिनियम ने विधि सदस्य को गवर्नर जनरल की परिषद में शामिल किया था। अतः विकल्प 4 1858 के अधिनियम का प्रावधान नहीं है।

question: Which extremist leader became a symbol of martyrdom after his death in British custody? (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Mahatma Gandhi
Hasrat Mohani
Chandrashekhar Azad
Bhagat Singh
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Bhagat Singh

Explanation:
Bhagat Singh was a prominent Indian revolutionary who fought against British rule. He was arrested in 1929 for throwing a bomb in the Central Assembly in Delhi. He was tried for murder and conspiracy, and ultimately hanged on 23 March 1931 in Lahore Jail. His death established him as a martyr in the Indian freedom struggle. Bhagat Singh's sacrifice became a symbol of martyrdom for Indian youth and continues to inspire people today. His revolutionary activities and ideas remain influential.

question: Which of the following Indian social classes initiated the Revolt of 1857? (RPF Constable 2024 (03/03/2025) Shift 3)
options: Soldiers (sepoys) and military personnel
British traders and merchants
Peasants and farmers
Zamindars
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Soldiers (sepoys) and military personnel

Explanation:
The Revolt of 1857 was a major uprising against British rule in India. It was initiated by soldiers (sepoys) and military personnel. The immediate cause was the introduction of greased cartridges rumored to be coated with cow and pig fat, which offended the religious sentiments of Hindu and Muslim sepoys. On May 10, 1857, sepoys at Meerut rebelled and marched to Delhi. While peasants, zamindars, and others later joined, the initial spark came from the sepoys. Hence, the correct option is soldiers and military personnel.
